subject: Pre-sales: dedicated fleet scaling workbook & API concurrency snapshot
messages:
From: James Hsu <james@acme-ai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot sizing — sample traffic and asks

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. We're planning a 3-month pilot (customer-facing assistant) and need a dedicated cluster recommendation and an outline of the preflight deliverables so procurement/sre know what to expect. Quick snapshot attached (acme_token_hist.csv + dayparting PDF). Key highlights: 
- Current production (managed infra): average prompt length: 42 tokens, average completion length: 260 tokens.
- Typical session pattern: short prompt + long completion (many code & doc generation flows).
- Baseline steady-state qps: 75 requests/min (1.25 RPS) over 18-hour business window; expected user growth during pilot: 5–7x by week 6.
- Observed peaks: single-day burst up to 6,200 completions (24h) around marketing events; realtime spikes reach ~1,600 concurrent active sessions in extreme load tests.
- KV cache hit estimated at ~18% on current implementation (no dedicated prefix caching yet).

Constraints: we need data-isolated tenancy (can't share pools with other customers) and an SLA of p95 latency < 700ms for short-form completions, and p99 for long-run completions best-effort. Procurement wants a ballpark cost estimate to compare to internal infra.

Can you confirm what additional telemetry you need? Also please include a short mutual action plan and a target date for a sizing workshop.

Thanks,
James
Director of Product — Acme AI
Attachments: acme_token_hist.csv (CSV, 220KB); acme_dayparting_summary.pdf (PDF, 130KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: James Hsu <james@acme-ai.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-ai.com
Date: 2026-11-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing — sample traffic and asks

Hi James — appreciate the detail, this is exactly the right level to start. Quick clarifying questions and next steps below.

Questions (short):
1) Do you expect prompt length distribution to shift (e.g., more short prompts / longer completions) as you ramp? Any top-10 prompt templates you can share (redact PII)?
2) For the observed 1,600 concurrent active sessions test: were those sessions issuing streaming responses or single-shot completions? If streaming, what's the average tokens/second output?
3) Does Acme require on-prem or VPC Private deployment for the pilot, or will Dedicated (isolated pool in Redwood infra) suffice?

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and timeline: 
- Today: confirm answers above + upload a 48-hour token-level trace (sample) — we can use that to build a synthetic replay.
- Within 3 business days: sizing workshop (1 hour) w/ you + SRE + product (we'll invite Karthik + Soojin).
- Within 5 business days: Redwood provides an initial sizing workbook (GPU SKUs, concurrency guardrails, cost ballpark) and an action checklist.
- Week 2: optional stress-run in our sandbox to validate latency assumptions; iterate on batching/quantization knobs.

I've attached our preflight template (redwood-preflight-template.xlsx) — fill the highlighted sections if possible. For the workshop, propose Wed 11/10 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 11/11 14:00–15:00 PT. Which works?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-preflight-template.xlsx (XLSX, 320KB)

Karthik / Soojin — forwarding Acme's snapshot. Can you review and bring a rough sizing for the workshop? High-level asks:
- Data-isolated dedicated pool; support streaming completions and long responses.
- Peak concurrency tested ~1,600 active sessions (need to assume headroom x1.5 for safety unless we fit a burst policy).
- Average prompt 42 tokens, average completion 260 tokens; dayparting shows ~6x uplift during events.

Specific items to prepare:
- Quick SKU recommendation (e.g., 4x80GB A100 vs N x 48GB Ampere) and why.
- A simple throughput calc: tokens/sec requirement -> tokens/sec per GPU -> number GPUs. Use conservative KV-cache hit 18% and plan for enabling prefix caching (estimate savings).
- Cost ballpark for 3-month pilot + optional stress validation run costs.

I'll schedule the workshop for Wed 11/10 10:00 PT unless you object.

—Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot sizing — sample traffic and asks (initial sizing)

Marissa / Soojin — quick first-pass that we can bring as a starting point to the workshop. Assumptions are conservative; we'll refine after the 48-hour token trace and a short sandbox replay.

Summary (initial):
- Workload: avg prompt 42 tokens + avg completion 260 tokens -> ~302 tokens per request. Streaming for long completions (token-by-token) assumed at 15 tokens/s on average during completion windows.
- Steady-state RPS during pilot (week 1): 1.25 RPS -> expected ramp to 7 RPS (5–7x) by week 6. Plan for peak-day event: short window spikes up to 50 RPS sustained for minutes and stress spikes to 200 RPS (synthetic).

Throughput calc (simple):
- Tokens/sec @ steady ramp target (7 RPS): 7 * 302 ≈ 2114 tokens/sec.
- Peak stress target (200 RPS): 200 * 302 = 60,400 tokens/sec.

GPU sizing (conservative):
- For model variant (Llama-3-class 34B FP16-equivalent) we estimate ~11,000 tokens/sec per 80GB A100 when using optimized kernels + continuous batching for this prompt shape (long completions; KV cache low).
- To meet steady ramp (2,114 t/s) → 1 GPU sufficient headroom; to meet peak stress (60,400 t/s) → ~6 GPUs.
- Given concurrency headroom, recommended initial Dedicated pool: 8x80GB-class GPUs (allows: handling stress spikes, canary + one spare for maintenance, and headroom for dayparting spikes).

Operational notes / cost guardrails:
- Enable prefix/KV caching (expected to improve token demand by ~15–30% depending on repetition patterns). If hit rate increases to 40% after engineering changes, peak GPU need drops to ~4–5 GPUs.
- Recommend 2-week canary with autoscale policy: base pool 2 GPUs, scale step +2 GPUs when sustained token/sec > 8,000 for 3 minutes, max cap 10 GPUs for pilot.
- Suggest we offer a pilot discount line-item and include one free stress-validation run in our sandbox (2 hours).

Deliverables for workshop:
- Sizing workbook with worst-case and expected-case columns (I'll produce).
- Runbook excerpt for burst routing + model fallback to smaller quantized variant if latency p99 > 1.5s.
- Cost estimate (3-month): rough internal calc attached in the copy we'll send to procurement during the workshop.

If no objections, I'll convert this into the workbook for Wed 11/10.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
